title: Christmas Pudding
subtitle: The traditional rich, aged, brandied pudding for Christmas Day
excerpt: A dense, dark pudding of dried fruit, suet, spice, and brandy, made weeks ahead and steamed for 6 hours, then aged and fed with brandy before a 2-hour reheat on Christmas Day.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (1861), Elizabeth David, and Delia Smith all give the foundation mix. The tradition of making the pudding on Stir-Up Sunday (the last Sunday before Advent) and feeding it with brandy through November appears in English cookbooks since at least the 1700s. The 6-hour initial steam is consistent across all classic sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after the initial 6-hour steam, once completely cooled. Wrap in the original parchment and foil, then in a freezer bag. Thaw in the fridge overnight. Steam for 2 hours to reheat on Christmas Day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 3 weeks ahead (traditionally on Stir-Up Sunday in November). Once the initial steam is complete and the pudding is cool, feed with 1 tablespoon of brandy poured through small holes in the base once a week. Store in a cool, dark cupboard.

content.text: Christmas pudding is a dense, dark pudding of dried fruit, suet, breadcrumbs, spice, and brandy, made weeks ahead of Christmas and aged with weekly brandy feeds. The long initial steam, 6 hours, sets the pudding and fuses the ingredients; the weeks of rest deepen the flavour until it is almost entirely unlike anything you could make in an afternoon. On Christmas Day, a further 2-hour steam is all it needs.

In a very large bowl, combine all the dry ingredients: sultanas, currants, raisins, mixed peel, suet, breadcrumbs, flour, sugar, and spices. Stir well so everything is evenly distributed. Add the beaten eggs, treacle, and brandy. Mix thoroughly with a large wooden spoon, the traditional rule is that every member of the household stirs once from east to west and makes a wish. The mixture should be stiff and fragrant.

Grease a 1.2-litre pudding basin well with butter. Spoon in the mixture and press it down firmly, there should be no air pockets. The pudding should fill the basin to about 2cm below the rim, to allow for some expansion. Cut a circle of baking paper and place it directly on the surface of the pudding. Cover with a double layer of baking paper and a layer of foil, all pleated across the middle to allow for expansion. Tie tightly with string around the rim and make a handle across the top.

Lower the basin into a large pan of boiling water. The water should come halfway up the sides of the basin. Cover the pan tightly and steam over a medium-low heat for 6 hours. The water must be kept at a steady simmer throughout, check every 45 minutes and top up with boiling water as needed. Do not let the pan boil dry. After 6 hours the pudding will be very dark, firm, and fragrant.

Lift the basin from the pan and leave until completely cool. Remove the damp parchment and replace with fresh dry parchment and foil, tied as before. Store in a cool, dark cupboard. Once a week, pierce the base of the pudding with a skewer in several places and spoon over 1 tablespoon of brandy. Re-cover after each feed.

On Christmas Day, steam the pudding again for 2 hours, exactly as before, with the basin in boiling water coming halfway up the sides. Turn out onto a warm plate. To flame, warm a ladleful of brandy in a small pan until it just begins to steam, then pour over the pudding and light with a long match. Serve with brandy butter, clotted cream, or custard.

items.symptom: The pudding sinks in the middle after turning out
items.cause: The basin was overfilled, or the steam was too vigorous at the start.
items.fix: Fill to no more than 2cm below the rim. Maintain a steady simmer rather than a rolling boil. A slight dip in the top is cosmetic only, the flavour is unaffected.

items.cause: Not enough brandy feeds, or the pudding was stored somewhere warm.
items.fix: Feed more generously each week. Store in a cool, dark place, not a warm kitchen cupboard. A cool pantry or garage shelf is ideal.

items.symptom: The pudding is not dark enough
items.cause: Insufficient treacle, or light muscovado was used instead of dark.
items.fix: Use dark muscovado and the full tablespoon of black treacle. The colour deepens further with each week of storage and with the Christmas Day steam.

content.text: Keeps in a cool, dark place for up to 3 months with weekly brandy feeding. Once cut, refrigerate the remainder and reheat portions by steaming in a covered bowl for 20 minutes. The pudding can also be frozen after the initial steam, see freezing note above.
